headline: Dry high pressure holds through Wednesday: mild Bluegrass afternoons and a Tuesday warm-up in the Upstate before a breezier, cloudier Wednesday
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: A broad surface high and midlevel ridge keep Danville and the Bluegrass dry through Wednesday. Some mid- and high-level cloud crosses the region today, but low levels remain dry and afternoon temperatures recover quickly. Tuesday is mostly sunny and mild. A weak, moisture-starved disturbance passing north of the area increases cloud and the southwest breeze Wednesday without generating meaningful rain. Clearer overnight periods still favor localized pre-dawn river-valley fog and isolated frost in the coldest sheltered spots.
kentucky.currentConditions: At 6:35 AM EDT, KDVK was clear at 41°F with a 39°F dew point, calm wind and visibility above 10 miles. The latest KLEX observation at 5:54 AM was 43°F with a 40°F dew point, a southeast wind at 3 kt, visibility above 10 miles and scattered-to-broken midlevel clouds from 6,000 to 12,000 feet. Neither station reported precipitation, and no official NWS alert was active for the Danville point at the 6:55 AM check.

days.label: Monday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for the Danville point. Independent concern is limited to patchy river-valley fog and isolated frost late tonight into Tuesday morning; a widespread freeze is not expected.
days.forecast: Intervals of mid- and high-level cloud give way to a partly to mostly sunny, mild afternoon as the dry surface ridge holds. Danville's most likely high is near 73°F with light west or variable wind. Tonight turns mostly clear and chilly with a most likely Danville low near 44°F; sheltered valleys may reach the upper 30s with patchy fog or frost toward Tuesday dawn.

days.label: Tuesday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for Tuesday at issuance. Independent concern remains limited to localized river-valley fog or frost late Tuesday night into Wednesday morning.
days.forecast: Any localized valley fog dissipates quickly, followed by mostly sunny and mild weather beneath the ridge. Danville's most likely high is near 74°F with a light southeast wind. Tuesday night is mostly clear to partly cloudy with a most likely low near 47°F; localized fog may redevelop in the most sheltered valleys before Wednesday dawn.

days.label: Wednesday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for Wednesday at issuance, and no significant independent hazard is expected. Localized late-night valley fog remains possible, but increasing cloud may limit it.
days.forecast: A weak shortwave passing north of Kentucky brings more mid- and high-level cloud and a modest southwest breeze, but the lower atmosphere remains too dry for meaningful precipitation. Danville's most likely high is near 74°F. Wednesday night has a most likely low near 45°F, with only a limited localized valley-fog risk before the forecast ends Thursday morning.

kentucky.bottomLine: Central Kentucky stays dry through Wednesday. Most likely Danville highs are near 73°F, 74°F and 74°F, with most likely nighttime lows near 44°F, 47°F and 45°F. Localized pre-dawn valley fog or frost remains possible, while Wednesday brings more cloud and a slightly stronger southwest breeze without meaningful rain.
kentucky.confidence: High on dry weather and daytime temperatures; moderate-high on nighttime temperatures and moderate on exact midlevel-cloud coverage and localized valley fog

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson primary · Central/Pickens County comparison
upstate.summary: A 1,030-mb surface high north of the Carolinas maintains a shallow, dry northeast-flow wedge today. Very dry air above roughly 925 mb supports abundant sunshine despite the cool near-surface flow. The wedge weakens Tuesday, allowing the warmest afternoon of the period. A reinforcing continental air mass strengthens northeast flow and adds cloud Wednesday, but the column remains too dry for rain.
upstate.currentConditions: At 5:54 AM EDT, KCEU was clear at 52°F with a 46°F dew point, a north wind at 4 kt and visibility above 10 miles. At 6:35 AM, KLQK was clear at 40°F with a 38°F dew point, calm wind and visibility above 10 miles. The 12-degree station split highlights local terrain and cold-air drainage. No official NWS alert was active for Clemson or Central at the 6:55 AM checks. Tempest data was not used.

days.label: Monday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for Clemson or Central. The NWS GSP morning package's Frost Advisory applies only to parts of western North Carolina north of the corridor. Independent concern is limited to isolated frost in the coldest sheltered Pickens County locations late tonight; a corridor freeze is not expected.
days.forecast: The shallow dry wedge gradually weakens under sunshine, with a most likely Clemson high near 72°F. Northeast wind stays light at 0–5 mph with gusts around 5–12 mph. Tonight is clear and chilly with a most likely Clemson low near 46°F; sheltered Central and Pickens County locations may approach 38°F with isolated frost.

days.label: Tuesday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for Tuesday at issuance, and no significant independent hazard is expected as the shallow cool dome weakens.
days.forecast: Sunny and warmer as the wedge relaxes, with a most likely Clemson high near 75°F. North to northeast wind remains light at 0–5 mph with gusts around 5–12 mph. Tuesday night stays mostly clear with a most likely Clemson low near 49°F; colder sheltered locations around Central may reach the lower 40s.

days.label: Wednesday
days.hazard: No official NWS alert is active for Wednesday at issuance. Independent concern is a reinforcing northeast breeze with gusts around 15–24 mph, remaining below advisory and verification-hazard thresholds.
days.forecast: A reinforcing continental air mass turns the low-level flow more firmly northeast. Wednesday becomes partly sunny and then mostly cloudy with a most likely Clemson high near 72°F. Northeast wind increases to 5–10 mph with gusts around 15–24 mph. The air column remains dry, and Wednesday night's most likely Clemson low is near 53°F.

upstate.bottomLine: The Clemson–Central corridor remains dry through Wednesday. Most likely Clemson highs are near 72°F, 75°F and 72°F, with most likely lows near 46°F, 49°F and 53°F. The shallow wedge weakens Tuesday, then northeast flow and cloud increase Wednesday; no local official alert or threshold hazard is expected.
upstate.confidence: High on dry weather; moderate-high on Monday and Tuesday temperatures, and moderate on Wednesday cloud coverage, daytime temperature and the strength of the reinforcing northeast breeze

sourceNotes: No official NWS alert was active for the Danville, Clemson or Central point at the final 10:55:23Z checks. The Frost Advisory described in the Greenville-Spartanburg morning package was confined to parts of western North Carolina outside the Clemson–Central corridor; official alerts remain separate from this independent analysis.

The final official-data retrieval at 10:55:23Z returned 10:35Z KDVK/KLQK observations; the latest available KLEX/KCEU reports remained 09:54Z. Observation times—not retrieval time—are preserved in the source entries and current-conditions text.

The 06:53Z Louisville and 05:20Z Greenville-Spartanburg discussions, current point forecasts, observations and the complete synthesis agree on a dry 72-hour period. The GSP discussion supports a shallow dry wedge, Tuesday warming and a reinforcing continental northeast flow Wednesday.

The locally extracted seven-model package was generated at 10:48:37Z and passed guidance validation with all seven requested models available: 268 files, 9,332 decoded GRIB messages, 241 extracted records and 36 station proposals.

The ECMWF 06Z +78-hour index returned 404 at the fixed 10:00Z availability cutoff, so the fresh, complete 00Z official cycle was selected. It extends through 12Z October 29 and was 10 hours 57 minutes old at candidate issuance, within the 12-hour freshness limit.
HRRR ends at 06Z October 28, NAM 3-km at 18Z October 28 and RAP at 12Z October 28. Their normal partial horizons are disclosed in model status and partial Upstate benchmarks rather than extrapolated.

For the pipeline's 10Z October 29 cutoff, exact QPF gaps were zero for GFS, 1 hour for ECMWF/NAM, 4 hours for GEFS, 16 hours for NAM 3-km and 22 hours for HRRR/RAP. Candidate validity extends 57 minutes beyond that cutoff, so each gap is 57 minutes longer; all available QPF increments, official forecasts and independent point/ensemble sources remain dry, so this is a disclosed cadence/horizon edge rather than a material conflict.

Fresh Kentucky GRIB guidance keeps highs tightly clustered near the lower 70s Monday and Tuesday, then shows a wider 70–75°F spread Wednesday as cloud increases. The KDVK station corrections and official point guidance were applied to the narrower most-likely Danville values inside the calibrated regional ranges.

Kentucky fog support is localized and timing-sensitive: short-range guidance supports pre-dawn valley fog, while the NAM-only dense KLEX signal Tuesday and Wednesday is not a corridor-wide consensus. Probabilities and windows remain explicitly localized.

Upstate GFS, ECMWF and GEFS values are direct Clemson-area point or ensemble guidance with provider cycle opacity disclosed. NAM, NAM 3-km, HRRR and RAP values are explicitly labeled KGSP BUFKIT proxies; partial high-only records are identified and never treated as full-day station forecasts.

The newly installed BUFKIT 19 application and its active KLEX setup under C:\Users\Public\Bufkit were verified as functional. The active files had last been refreshed with October 24 cycles and exceeded the 36-hour freshness limit at this candidate's October 26 issuance, so fresh October 26 KLEX and KGSP Warehouse/archive profiles cached for this run were used instead. The historical sample files under Program Files were not the active dataset or forecast inputs. BUFKIT remains a visualization interface for underlying model cycles, not an additional model.

NWS KLVX and KGSP radar showed no precipitation near either region. College of DuPage Ohio River Valley radar and clean-infrared imagery supported the dry pattern; Southeast infrared imagery showed a clear/dry sector. The unavailable College of DuPage Southeast radar product was not interpreted or claimed.

Chris Bailey's exact October 26 Kentucky Weather Center post, “Big Changes to Start November,” supports highs around 70–75°F, cool nights and good weather through Halloween. Its rain and storm change begins beyond this 72-hour forecast and was excluded.

The latest cumulative accuracy summary was consulted: 83 verified checkpoints and 77.3% all-category accuracy overall, including 81.6% for Central Kentucky and 73.1% for the Upstate. Updated station corrections, calibrated widths, regime-specific weights, fog timing, wind ranges and official-alert handling were applied.

Temperature cards retain calibrated regional coverage widths, while prose gives narrower most-likely Danville and Clemson point values. The wider overnight ranges represent the verified KCEU–KLQK and KDVK–valley terrain spread, not uncertainty at one exact point.
